name: Valley of Flowers Trek
summary: Walk through alpine meadows in full bloom and climb to the glacial lake at Hemkund Sahib.
description:
The Valley of Flowers is a high-altitude national park in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. During the monsoon its meadows fill with hundreds of species of wildflowers, from blue poppies to cobra lilies, framed by waterfalls and snowy peaks.
From Rishikesh we drive to Joshimath (Jyotirmath) and Govindghat, then walk up to the village of Ghangaria, our base for a full day in the valley and a climb to Gurdwara Hemkund Sahib, which sits beside a glacial lake at over 4,600 metres. Expect 10 to 14 kilometres of steady walking on trekking days. Guesthouse stays, meals and park permits are included.

name: Kedarkantha Winter Trek
summary: A snow trek through pine forest to a summit with views across the Garhwal Himalaya.
description:
Kedarkantha is one of the best-known winter treks in India. The trail climbs from the village of Sankri through pine and oak forest inside Govind Pashu Vihar National Park to open snowfields and a summit at around 3,800 metres, with views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch and Black Peak.
We drive from Dehradun to Sankri, camp at Juda Ka Talab and the Kedarkantha base, and leave for the summit before dawn. Tents, sleeping bags, microspikes and all meals on the trail are included. You should be comfortable walking for five to seven hours a day with a light pack.

name: Ladakh High Passes
summary: Cross some of the highest roads in the world to Nubra's dunes and the blue water of Pangong Tso.
description:
Ladakh is a high-altitude desert of monasteries, river valleys and mountain passes above 5,000 metres. This trip starts with two unhurried days in Leh, at around 3,500 metres, so your body can adjust before we go higher.
From Leh we cross Khardung La into the Nubra Valley, visit Diskit Monastery and the sand dunes and Bactrian camels at Hunder, then follow the Shyok river to the shore of Pangong Tso. We return over Chang La and finish at Hemis Monastery. Permits, a dedicated vehicle and driver, oxygen on board and an experienced local guide are included.

name: Spiti Valley Star Gazer
summary: High desert villages, old monasteries and some of the darkest night skies in India.
description:
Spiti is a cold desert valley in Himachal Pradesh, cut off by snow for half the year. Its high villages, thin dry air and almost no light pollution make it one of the best places in India to see the Milky Way with the naked eye.
We drive from Manali through the Atal Tunnel to the crescent-shaped lake of Chandra Taal, then over Kunzum Pass to Kaza. From there we visit Key Monastery, Kibber, Langza, Hikkim and Komic, with telescope sessions on clear nights. Homestays, meals, a vehicle with driver and permits are included.

name: Kerala Backwaters and Hills
summary: Old Fort Kochi, misty tea hills in Munnar and a night on a houseboat in the backwaters.
description:
Kerala fits very different landscapes into a short distance. This trip starts among the Chinese fishing nets and spice warehouses of Fort Kochi, climbs into the tea estates of Munnar and comes back down to the backwaters around Alappuzha and Vembanad Lake.
You will walk through a working tea estate, look for Nilgiri tahr in Eravikulam National Park, spend a night on a traditional kettuvallam houseboat and finish in Kumarakom. Hotels, the houseboat, all transfers and most meals are included.

name: Thar Desert Camel Safari
summary: A golden sandstone fort, an abandoned village and a night under the stars in the dunes.
description:
Jaisalmer rises out of the Thar Desert in western Rajasthan, and its sandstone fort is one of the few in the world where people still live inside the walls. It is part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After a day in the fort and the carved havelis of the old town, we visit the abandoned village of Kuldhara, then ride camels into the dunes at Sam for sunset, folk music and a night in a desert camp. Hotel and camp stays, camel rides and all meals are included.

name: Andaman Island Explorer
summary: White-sand beaches, coral reefs and the history of Port Blair across three islands.
description:
The Andaman Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, closer to Myanmar than to mainland India, with clear water, coral reefs and forest that runs down to the sand. We cover Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep), travelling between them by ferry.
Highlights include the Cellular Jail and its evening light and sound show, the ruins on Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep), sunset at Radhanagar Beach and a guided snorkelling trip off Havelock. No diving experience is needed. Hotels, ferries, transfers and breakfasts are included.

name: Golden Triangle Heritage
summary: Delhi, the Taj Mahal at sunrise and the pink city of Jaipur in one classic loop.
description:
The Golden Triangle links three of north India's great cities: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur. Between them they hold several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Humayun's Tomb, the Qutb Minar, the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.
We start in Old and New Delhi, drive to Agra for the fort and a sunrise visit to the Taj Mahal, stop at Fatehpur Sikri on the way to Jaipur and finish with Amber Fort, the City Palace and Hawa Mahal. The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays, so every departure is timed around it. Hotels, an air-conditioned vehicle, monument tickets and breakfasts are included.

name: Darjeeling and Sikkim Tea Trails
summary: Sunrise over Kangchenjunga, the toy train and tea estates across Darjeeling and Sikkim.
description:
Tea has been grown on the steep slopes around Darjeeling since the 1800s, and on a clear morning Kangchenjunga, the third-highest mountain in the world, fills the northern sky. This trip pairs tea estates and tastings with monasteries, mountain views and the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
From Darjeeling we ride the toy train to Ghum and around the Batasia Loop, cross into Sikkim for Pelling and Pemayangtse Monastery, walk through Temi Tea Garden and finish in Gangtok with Tsomgo Lake and Rumtek Monastery. Hotels, transfers, permits, the toy train, breakfasts and dinners are included.

name: Ranthambore Tiger Safari
summary: Four jeep safaris in one of the best places in India to see a wild tiger.
description:
Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan is a dry forest of lakes, ravines and old ruins, and one of the best places in India to see Bengal tigers in the wild. Leopards, sloth bears, crocodiles, sambar deer and more than 300 species of birds share the park.
We stay in Sawai Madhopur and go on four safaris, mornings and afternoons, in a private jeep with an expert naturalist. Between drives we walk up to Ranthambore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inside the park. Sightings are never guaranteed, and the park is closed from July to September. Lodge stay, safaris and meals are included.

name: Meghalaya Living Root Bridges
summary: Walk down to the double-decker root bridge at Nongriat and boat on the clear Umngot river.
description:
In the wet hills of Meghalaya, Khasi villagers have trained the roots of rubber fig trees across streams for generations, growing bridges that get stronger with age. The most famous, the double-decker bridge at Nongriat, sits at the bottom of a steep stairway of about 3,500 steps.
From Shillong we head to Sohra (Cherrapunji), one of the wettest places on earth, and Nohkalikai Falls, then walk down to Nongriat for a night in a village homestay. The trip ends at Mawlynnong and the clear Umngot river at Dawki. Homestays, hotels, transfers and meals are included. Expect rain at any time of year.

name: Hampi Ruins and Boulders
summary: Temples, royal ruins and giant boulders in the old capital of the Vijayanagara empire.
description:
Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire and, in the early 1500s, one of the largest cities in the world. Its ruins spread across a landscape of granite boulders, banana plantations and the Tungabhadra river, and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
We explore the Virupaksha Temple, the Royal Enclosure, the Lotus Mahal and the Vittala Temple with its stone chariot, partly by bicycle. Mornings start early for sunrise from Matanga Hill, and afternoons include a coracle ride on the river and the climb up Anjanadri Hill. Expect several hours of walking and scrambling each day. Guesthouse stays, bicycles, entry tickets and breakfasts are included.

name: Rishikesh Ganga Rafting
summary: White-water rafting on the Ganga, the evening aarti and the Beatles Ashram in three days.
description:
Rishikesh sits where the Ganga leaves the Himalayan foothills, and the stretch of river above the town is the best-known rafting run in India. Between September and June the water is clear and cold, with rapids such as Roller Coaster and Golf Course on the run down from Shivpuri.
After a safety briefing and a practice session, we raft about 16 kilometres from Shivpuri back towards Rishikesh with certified river guides. The rest of the trip is gentler: the evening aarti at Triveni Ghat, the bridges and cafes around Ram Jhula and a morning walk through the Beatles Ashram. Hotel, rafting, equipment and meals are included. You need to be comfortable in water while wearing a life jacket.
